en: The Jātaka:
Catukkanipāta, Kokilavagga (The Chapter on the Cuckoo)
10. The Viṣayahajātakam:
“In former times you gave gifts with effort;
yet for you who were giving, there was the nature of exhaustion.”
If one were not to give gifts from this point forward,
those riches would remain for the sake of self-restraint.
O thousand-eyed one, it is ignoble for an Ariya—
"Even in great distress, they say it is not a duty [to abandon faith];
O King of Gods, let that wealth not be yours,
for the sake of which we might abandon our faith."
Where one chariot goes,
there another chariot goes;
this is the ancient, established way.
Only what exists, O Vāsava, can be given.
If it will exist, we shall give;
if it does not exist, what can we give?
“Even though we have become such as this, we shall still give;
let us not withhold our gifts.
Thus ends the tenth Jātaka, the Visayha-jātaka.
The fourth chapter, the Kokila-vagga.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
Ativelapabhāsati and Jītavara.
The bull among charioteers, moving slowly through the midst of the forest,
then [saw] a Jambu tree, a grass seat, an excellent throne,
then rice, peacocks, and ten [other things] within his range.
